headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist by default; TREK’s MCP/collaborative surfaces can amplify RD-Agent’s broad egress and browser use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK exposes MCP and real-time collaborative inputs, while RD-Agent can run browsers and ingest external content. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK content is forwarded into RD-Agent or vice versa. No direct shared channel is documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF TREK MCP messages are forwarded into RD-Agent prompts without sanitization
IF RD-Agent browser-sourced text is copied into TREK collaborative sessions
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt forwarding between agents
Add a strict allowlist for MCP message types
Strip instructions from browser-sourced text before reuse
Require human review for any cross-agent copy-paste
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all shared content

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches reservations, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while RD-Agent has broad network egress and calls third-party APIs. If TREK data reaches RD-Agent, exfiltration risk is immediate and potentially irreversible. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible even without a documented shared filesystem, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF TREK secrets or reservation data are passed into RD-Agent context
IF RD-Agent is allowed to send prompts or files to external APIs during the same session
mitigations: Do not pass secrets between agents
Separate credentials per agent
Block RD-Agent egress for sensitive sessions
Redact confirmation numbers and MFA secrets before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and TREK is real-time collaborative while RD-Agent has file/log outputs and broad API use. Overlapping mutable activity can conflict on shared resources if orchestrated together, but no shared writable directory or lockless git state is documented. That makes conflict plausible but not proven at high severity.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or database
IF TREK collaborative edits and RD-Agent file writes target the same records
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Keep RD-Agent read-only for shared artifacts
Review concurrent edits before merge
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative planner with AI built in, and RD-Agent is a research/automation agent that can browse and use external APIs. If RD-Agent outputs are treated as authoritative by TREK, bad facts can cascade into user-facing plans or actions. Because the interaction is plausible in default collaborative workflows and downstream harm can be broad, high is warranted.
conditions: IF TREK consumes RD-Agent outputs without verification
IF RD-Agent-generated facts are used to update travel plans or reservations
mitigations: Require source links for every imported fact
Add a verification step before TREK displays RD-Agent content
Limit RD-Agent output to suggestions, not actions
Flag low-confidence claims for human review
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware downstream validation

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, email addresses, country visit history, API keys, and MFA secrets, while RD-Agent handles financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and external API calls. The pair therefore spans sensitive personal and operational data with different likely retention and residency expectations. No direct residency mismatch is documented, so medium fits the documented compliance gap.
conditions: IF TREK personal data is exported into RD-Agent logs or third-party APIs
IF retention policies differ for the same user records across the two systems
mitigations: Minimize shared personal data
Review retention settings in both systems
Disable logging of secrets and identifiers
Document data-flow boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
